Tell the human to install the matching SDK (`npm i -D @reticlehq/react@3.9.0 @reticlehq/vite-plugin@3.9.0`) or run `reticle update`, then restart their dev server so the page reloads with it. tools.name: reticle_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a pixel screenshot of the DRIVEN page (needs `reticle drive`/RETICLE_CDP_URL — the SDK has no screenshotter) and save it as a visual baseline at .reticle/visual/<name>.png. { fullPage } for the whole scroll height, { ref } or { clip:{x,y,width,height} } for one element/region. Returns { saved:true, name, path, bytes } or { ok:false, reason } when no driven browser is attached.

params.name: name
params.description: Baseline name — saved as .reticle/visual/<name>.png. Use the same name in reticle_visual_diff to compare.

params.name: fullPage
params.description: Capture the full scroll height. Default: viewport only.

params.name: ref
params.description: Element ref to screenshot (scopes to element bounding box). Omit for full page.

params.name: clip
params.description: Explicit { x, y, width, height } clip rectangle in page coordinates.

params.name: sessionId
params.description: OMIT THIS unless you mean a specific tab — Reticle scopes to your project, prefers the active one, and refuses rather than guesses when ambiguous. Pass an id from reticle_sessions only to target a particular tab. The previous wording ("omit when only ONE session is open") was wrong and cost real turns: with three sessions connected — an app plus two pool leases — resolution is still unambiguous, but that sentence sent the agent off to list and filter sessions by hand before every single call.

tools.name: reticle_look
tools.description: Read the page, by action: "page" is the semantic snapshot of what is rendered, "find" resolves a locator (testid/role/text/component) to refs you can act on, "element" is the full detail of one ref, "state" reads the framework store. Reads only — nothing here changes the app.

params.name: action
params.description: Which operation to run. Omit for "page".

params.name: scope
params.description: CSS selector or element ref to restrict the snapshot to a subtree. Omit to snapshot the whole page.

params.name: mode
params.description: full = all elements; interactive = only clickable/focusable elements; status = only route + title. Default: full.

params.name: diff
params.description: Return only what changed since your last snapshot of the same scope/mode (mode:delta|unchanged). First call (or after a route change) still returns the full tree.

params.name: ids
params.description: Add [testid=…] to each control that carries one: a stable identity for a harness mapping the app. Off by default; it costs tokens.

params.name: audit
params.description: Also measure the page for what a person would see broken: text cut off with no ellipsis, controls drawn over each other, text under WCAG contrast. Returns `audit: [{ kind, ref, what, detail }]`. Off by default; it forces layout.

params.name: sessionId
params.description: OMIT THIS unless you mean a specific tab — Reticle scopes to your project, prefers the active one, and refuses rather than guesses when ambiguous. Pass an id from reticle_sessions only to target a particular tab. The previous wording ("omit when only ONE session is open") was wrong and cost real turns: with three sessions connected — an app plus two pool leases — resolution is still unambiguous, but that sentence sent the agent off to list and filter sessions by hand before every single call.

params.name: by
params.description: Query strategy.

params.name: value
params.description: Query value for the selected strategy (e.g. by=role value=button, or by=testid value=submit-btn). Or use the predicate spelling directly: { testid: "submit" }, { text: "Deploy" }.

params.name: name
params.description: Exact accessible-name filter - narrows results when `by` is role and the page has many elements of that role. Matches the whole name; use `text` for a partial match.

params.name: self
params.description: Return the `scope` element ITSELF instead of searching inside it. Use when the target is a plain layout container with no role, name, testid or text of its own — which is routinely the element that carries the handler, and is otherwise unreachable because every query excludes its own scope root. Requires `scope`.

params.name: attrs
params.description: Attribute NAMES to return per match, e.g. ['href'] for links, ['src'] for images. Projects, never filters: 'name=value' is refused. Absent omitted; credentials redacted.

params.name: limit
params.description: Cap the returned descriptors to the first N (cuts tokens on broad queries). If more matched, the result carries total + truncated:true so the trim is never silent — narrow with name/scope.

params.name: count_only
params.description: Return just { count } (no element descriptors) — use when you only need "how many match?" and not their refs.

params.name: testid
params.description: Predicate spelling of by/value.

params.name: text
params.description: Predicate spelling of by/value.

params.name: role
params.description: Predicate spelling of by/value.

params.name: label
params.description: Predicate spelling of by/value.

params.name: placeholder
params.description: Predicate spelling of by/value.

params.name: alt
params.description: Predicate spelling of by/value.

params.name: ref
params.description: Element ref (e.g. 'e42') from reticle_snapshot/reticle_query — stable until the element leaves the DOM, so no re-snapshot between actions.

params.name: store
params.description: Registered store name (e.g. 'workspace'). Omit to read all stores.

params.name: path
params.description: Dot-path into the store (e.g. 'captionCache.v3'). Numeric array indices are supported.

params.name: depth
params.description: Collapse anything deeper than N levels to a size marker — avoids huge outputs for large stores. A whole number of levels, 1 or more.

tools.name: reticle_assert
tools.description: Prove a consequence, by action: "now" evaluates a predicate against the window that already exists, "wait" waits for one to become true within a budget. Both return a verdict; only `verified:"yes"` is a pass. `screenshot.path` is a picture of the page at the outcome: open it when the look of the page matters; reading it is your choice. When `pending: true`, the file may still be in write; wait before you read it.

params.name: action
params.description: Which operation to run. Omit for "now".

params.name: predicate
params.description: Predicate to evaluate. Kinds: { signal, name|dataMatches|count } { net, urlContains|method|status|count|bodyMatches|bodyContains|requestBodyContains|requestBodyMatches } { state, path|equals } { route, pathname (exact) | contains (path+query+hash) } { element, testid|role|text } { text } { console, level|contains|absent } { animation, name } { settled } { compare, left, right } — combine with { allOf | anyOf | not }. Prefer a signal/net/state consequence over element/text presence. For net and signal, count is exact; omit it for at least one; 0 means never.

params.name: until
params.description: Alias for `predicate` (act_and_wait's name).

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description: If > 0, wait up to this many milliseconds before failing. Default: 0 (evaluate once). Capped at 55000: your MCP client aborts the request before a longer wait can return, so a bound above this would be advertised and not deliverable. To outlast it, poll — several short waits, each of which returns a verdict.

params.name: since
params.description: Cursor from a prior reticle_act — scopes the assertion to events after that act.

params.name: intent
params.description: What this change is meant to make true — as a durable statement ABOUT THE PRODUCT, or the id of an intent you already declared. Write it so a teammate who was not here understands it in six months: name the behaviour, not this run. GOOD: "a filtered issue queue is a shareable link — the filter is in the URL". BAD: "P1 step 5", "drive 2 of 2", "same as before the fix", "the board renders cleanly" — these name a session, a step number or nothing checkable, and the person reading them later has none of that context. This is shared memory: it is pooled per project and later agents read it back to avoid re-deriving what you just established. Recorded in .reticle/intent/, the same ledger reticle_intent writes, and marked proved by this verdict if it passes.

params.name: sessionId
params.description: OMIT THIS unless you mean a specific tab — Reticle scopes to your project, prefers the active one, and refuses rather than guesses when ambiguous. Pass an id from reticle_sessions only to target a particular tab. The previous wording ("omit when only ONE session is open") was wrong and cost real turns: with three sessions connected — an app plus two pool leases — resolution is still unambiguous, but that sentence sent the agent off to list and filter sessions by hand before every single call.

params.name: detail
params.description: "compact" keeps only the deciding fields.

params.name: action
params.description: Which operation to run. Omit for "now".

params.name: predicate
params.description: Predicate to evaluate. Kinds: { signal, name|dataMatches|count } { net, urlContains|method|status|count|bodyMatches|bodyContains|requestBodyContains|requestBodyMatches } { state, path|equals } { route, pathname (exact) | contains (path+query+hash) } { element, testid|role|text } { text } { console, level|contains|absent } { animation, name } { settled } { compare, left, right } — combine with { allOf | anyOf | not }. Prefer a signal/net/state consequence over element/text presence. For net and signal, count is exact; omit it for at least one; 0 means never.

params.name: until
params.description: Alias for `predicate` (act_and_wait's name).

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description: If > 0, wait up to this many milliseconds before failing. Default: 0 (evaluate once). Capped at 55000: your MCP client aborts the request before a longer wait can return, so a bound above this would be advertised and not deliverable. To outlast it, poll — several short waits, each of which returns a verdict.

params.name: since
params.description: Cursor from a prior reticle_act — scopes the assertion to events after that act.

params.name: intent
params.description: What this change is meant to make true — as a durable statement ABOUT THE PRODUCT, or the id of an intent you already declared. Write it so a teammate who was not here understands it in six months: name the behaviour, not this run. GOOD: "a filtered issue queue is a shareable link — the filter is in the URL". BAD: "P1 step 5", "drive 2 of 2", "same as before the fix", "the board renders cleanly" — these name a session, a step number or nothing checkable, and the person reading them later has none of that context. This is shared memory: it is pooled per project and later agents read it back to avoid re-deriving what you just established. Recorded in .reticle/intent/, the same ledger reticle_intent writes, and marked proved by this verdict if it passes.

params.name: sessionId
params.description: OMIT THIS unless you mean a specific tab — Reticle scopes to your project, prefers the active one, and refuses rather than guesses when ambiguous. Pass an id from reticle_sessions only to target a particular tab. The previous wording ("omit when only ONE session is open") was wrong and cost real turns: with three sessions connected — an app plus two pool leases — resolution is still unambiguous, but that sentence sent the agent off to list and filter sessions by hand before every single call.

args.intent: Workers can switch to the access link form and enter a one-time token.

result.next: Done driving? reticle_session { action: "yield" } hands the tab back.
result.because: assertion held at presence grade with no channel disagreeing, but coverage was PARTIAL — see `coverage` for what went unobserved

instrumentationGaps.missing: this app declared no capabilities at all, so no state can be read from it
instrumentationGaps.cost: every verdict here rests on what the DOM happens to show, and reticle_state will stay empty however many flows are driven
instrumentationGaps.fix: import { registerStore } from '@reticlehq/browser' and call registerStore(name, store) with a subscribable store so its changes are observed; a bare getter is readable but does not report changes. For component-local React state, import { useReticleStore } from '@reticlehq/react/store' and call useReticleStore(name, value), assert the DOM, or read it with reticle_look { action: 'state', ref: '...' }

engineBlindSpots.detail: the claim "Workers can switch to the access link form and enter a one-time token." states an amount, and no verdict ran a computed comparison against it

result.advice: This predicate only checks element/text presence, not an observable consequence. A locator healed to the wrong element (or a stale render) can satisfy it while the feature is broken. Prefer a { signal } or { net } assertion (or allOf it with one) so green means the feature actually worked.

tools.name: reticle_act_and_wait
tools.description: Act on a ref, then wait for a predicate to hold — one hop for the act->observe->assert loop. Omit `until` to wait for the page to settle (network + DOM idle) — use this instead of a fixed sleep. Returns { effect } (the action result), { verdict } (predicate pass/evidence/near-miss), { trace } (a digest — window_ms + summary counts of what the app did), and { since } (the act cursor; pass it to reticle_observe for the full per-event timeline when the counts are not enough). timeout_ms 0 evaluates the predicate once without waiting. `screenshot.path` is a picture of the page at the outcome: open it when the look of the page matters; reading it is your choice. When `pending: true`, the file may still be in write; wait before you read it.

params.name: ref
params.description: Element ref (e.g. 'e42') from reticle_snapshot/reticle_query — stable until the element leaves the DOM, so no re-snapshot between actions. Give this OR `target`. A press of Escape, Tab, or a modifier shortcut (Cmd+K) is a document key and needs neither.

params.name: target
params.description: Find the element and act on it in ONE call, instead of a reticle_query round trip first: { testid } | { text } | { role, name } | { label }. Refuses if it matches more than one, rather than guessing.

params.name: action
params.description: Action to perform.

params.name: args
params.description: Action-specific arguments: { value } for fill/select (select also drives an ARIA combobox: it opens it and clicks the option by its label), { text } for type/press (the key NAME, e.g. Escape or Tab), { modifiers: ["Meta","Shift"] } for a press shortcut or a click (Meta/Control/Shift/Alt), { button: "right" | "middle" } for a click, { toRef } for drag (the ref to drop ON — without it the drag lands nowhere), { confirmDangerous: true } for a potentially destructive control. For upload: { path } is a path on disk (absolute or relative to project root; daemon reads real bytes) or { name, content?, type? } for inline bytes.

params.name: predicate
params.description: Alias for `until`.

params.name: until
params.description: Predicate to wait for after the action completes (same shape as reticle_assert). OMIT to wait for the page to SETTLE — network + DOM idle — the deterministic default instead of a sleep. To assert a consequence AND settle, allOf them: { kind: "allOf", predicates: [<your predicate>, { kind: "settled" }] }.

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. 0 = evaluate once without waiting. Default: 4000.

params.name: refuseWhenThrottled
params.description: Throw if the tab is throttled. Default: false.

params.name: intent
params.description: What this change is meant to make true — as a durable statement ABOUT THE PRODUCT, or the id of an intent you already declared. Write it so a teammate who was not here understands it in six months: name the behaviour, not this run. GOOD: "a filtered issue queue is a shareable link — the filter is in the URL". BAD: "P1 step 5", "drive 2 of 2", "same as before the fix", "the board renders cleanly" — these name a session, a step number or nothing checkable, and the person reading them later has none of that context. This is shared memory: it is pooled per project and later agents read it back to avoid re-deriving what you just established. Recorded in .reticle/intent/, the same ledger reticle_intent writes, and marked proved by this verdict if it passes.

params.name: durable
params.description: After a yes, reload and require the element/text/state part of `until` to hold again.

params.name: sessionId
params.description: OMIT THIS unless you mean a specific tab — Reticle scopes to your project, prefers the active one, and refuses rather than guesses when ambiguous. Pass an id from reticle_sessions only to target a particular tab. The previous wording ("omit when only ONE session is open") was wrong and cost real turns: with three sessions connected — an app plus two pool leases — resolution is still unambiguous, but that sentence sent the agent off to list and filter sessions by hand before every single call.

params.name: detail
params.description: "compact" keeps only the deciding fields.

predicateGrammar.text: contains, visible, absent, scope, self, satisfies { property, values, of, tolerance, pattern, is, by }, ignoreCase
predicateGrammar.net: method, urlContains, status, ok, since, count, bodyContains, bodyMatches, requestBodyContains, requestBodyMatches, repeatable
predicateGrammar.state: store, path, equals, satisfies { property, values, of, tolerance, pattern, is, by }
predicateGrammar.compare: left { from, urlContains, method, body, path, name, store, scope }, right { from, urlContains, method, body, path, name, store, scope }, as, tolerance
